speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned sudden-onset vertigo; can you describe exactly how the spinning sensation started and how long it lasts? Also, have you experienced any hearing loss, ringing in your ears, or trouble speaking alongside this dizziness?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds like a classic episode of benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV). Since the dizziness resolved and you are back to your baseline, do you notice any specific head movements, like looking up or turning over in bed, that currently trigger the spinning sensation?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sudden-onset sensation of the room spinning. I also have Nausea, Vomiting, Dizziness.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV).
